content_preview.title: Linux Foundation Asks OSI to Approve OpenMDW-1.1 AI Model License as Reviewers Split Over Its Copyright Termination Clause
content_preview.summary: The Linux Foundation submitted its OpenMDW-1.1 AI model license to the Open Source Initiative for approval, but reviewers are contesting a clause that terminates rights over copyright lawsuits, not just patent ones.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The Linux Foundation has asked the Open Source Initiative (OSI) to formally approve its OpenMDW-1.1 license for distributing AI models, opening a public review that has already surfaced sharp disagreement over a clause that terminates a licensee's rights if they sue over copyright infringement, not just patents. [Michael Dolan](https://lists.opensource.org/pipermail/license-review_lists.opensource.org/2026-August/006125.html), the Linux Foundation's SVP of Legal & Strategic Programs...

recommendations: Before merging, the human reviewer should write a corrections file at src/content/corrections/<YYYY-MM>/<article-slug>.json documenting the warning(s).
Consider adding trusted domains to config/source_allowlist.txt

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Why It Matters). Neutral, precise legal reporting on a live OSI license-review thread; presents both the Linux Foundation's rationale and three independent objections (Fontana, Schultz, Chestek) without editorializing.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 5 sources fetched successfully (HTTP 200, no suspicious_patterns flags) and read from disk after gunzip; sha256 of each decompressed snapshot matches the manifest. source-0 (006125.html, Dolan's OSI submission incl. full license text) — confirms Aug 13 submission date, the MIT/Apache-2.0 comparison, the exact 'Apache-2.0's termination is limited to patent claims...' quote, the full termination clause text, the adoption list (NVIDIA 19 models/Cosmos/Ising/Nemotron, Arcee 6 Trinity models, Poolside Laguna S 2.1, BAAI OpenSeek Small, ByteDance Seed-X, IBM/Hartree SaltMarsh), and the SPDX status. source-1 (006126.html, Richard Fontana/Red Hat, confirmed via rfontana at redhat.com header) — every Fontana quote in the article (the 'seems to potentially go further...', the Apache-2.0/MPL-2.0/EPL-2.0 comparison, the Python-code hypothetical, the 'will need to specifically deliberate' line) is verbatim and correctly attributed to Fontana alone. source-2 (006135.html, Eric Schultz, confirmed via eric at wwahammy.com header and 'Digital Autonomy and Open Source activist' signature) — Schultz's quotes ('penalize them though...', 'amnesty for... large scale copyright infringement', 'stop trying to pretend like this is a brand new frontier') are verbatim and correctly attributed to Schultz, not conflated with the quoted Dolan follow-up reply embedded lower in the same page (the two Dolan quotes the article pulls from that page — 'The NVIDIA Open Model License terminates on copyright or patent litigation...' and 'I am not aware of any other AI model-focused license...' — are correctly attributed to Dolan, not Schultz). source-3 (006163.html, Pamela Chestek/Chestek Legal, confirmed via pamela at chesteklegal.com header and full signature block, posted Mon Aug 24 01:20 UTC matching the article's 'posted August 24') — every Chestek quote ('copyright infringement requires copying', 'volitional act (whether lawful or unlawful)', 'blanket immunity for that act', 'a completely non-culpable party has to give up a claim...', 'antithetical to open source principles', 'open source developers get exploited enough...', 'should be willing to defend the claim, not absolve themselves of liability through contract', 'opposed to version 1.1 because of the trigger of termination for a copyright infringement claim') is verbatim and correctly attributed to Chestek alone. source-4 (openmdw.ai homepage) — confirms the license's own self-description and general FAQ content; not directly quoted inline in the body.
editor_notes.misparaphrase_check: Specifically verified the submitting bot's claim that it caught and excluded a WebFetch mis-paraphrase ('fewer' vs. actual 'few'). Grepped all 5 decompressed snapshots for 'few'/'fewer': the only near-miss is in source-3 (Chestek's message, itself quoting/paraphrasing a clause about MIT sublicensing): 'a sublicensor can grant few of the rights than they obtained in the license' — an apparent grammatical slip in the source's own text (reads as if 'fewer... than' was intended). Confirmed this phrase does not appear anywhere in the article body — the bot correctly excluded it rather than 'fixing' or quoting it inaccurately.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Central thesis (LF submitted OpenMDW-1.1 to OSI; the copyright-termination clause is contested by named reviewers) is fully supported by source-0 through source-3. Two minor issues found, addressed via a corrections record rather than blocking publication: (1) the parenthetical 'OpenMDW — short for Open Model, Data, and Weights' in paragraph 2 does not appear in any of the 5 fetched snapshots (checked visible text and raw HTML/meta of openmdw.ai) — it is a plausible but source-unverified specific, not a headline/lead claim. (2) The license-clause quote 'files, maintains, or voluntarily participates in a lawsuit...' silently converts the source's second-person conditional ('If you file, maintain, or voluntarily participate...') to third-person to fit the sentence, inside quote marks — the substance of the clause is unchanged and the rest of the quoted clause is verbatim, but strictly speaking the opening words are not a verbatim reproduction.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral throughout; presents the Linux Foundation's defense (Dolan's industry-practice rationale, the NVIDIA Open Model License precedent) alongside all three critical positions without favoring either side. No sensationalism or loaded language.
editor_notes.originality: Checked src/content/articles/ for existing coverage of OpenMDW, OSI license review, or this mailing-list thread — no match. Related-but-distinct prior coverage exists (PHP's license change, European open-source adoption, NVIDIA Nemotron open-weight releases) but none overlaps this specific OSI review story. Genuinely new topic.
editor_notes.allowlist_gap: lists.opensource.org, opensource.org, and openmdw.ai were not on config/source_allowlist.txt at submission time (the automated script's only finding, which auto-downgraded the verdict from APPROVE to APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS). The submitting bot flagged this itself and deliberately left the allowlist untouched, treating it as out of scope for a submission PR. Judged on the merits: lists.opensource.org is OSI's own official public license-review mailing list — the primary venue for the exact process this article reports on — and opensource.org/openmdw.ai are the official sites of the OSI and the license project respectively. This is the same tier as the existing debian.org/lists.debian.org, lists.freebsd.org, and lists.gnu.org precedents already on the allowlist (official project/organization first-party channels used to report on that organization's own governance activity). Added all three domains to config/source_allowlist.txt in this review with a dated batch-addition comment following the established format, since this is a config file (not signed content) and squarely within Chief Editor remit. This resolves the allowlist gap going forward, but the verdict remains APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS on the independent merits of the two content issues found in factual_accuracy above.
concerns: Unsourced acronym expansion: 'OpenMDW — short for Open Model, Data, and Weights' does not appear in any of the 5 cited source snapshots.

Minor quote-fidelity issue: the termination-clause quote converts the source's second-person 'If you file, maintain, or voluntarily participate' to third-person 'files, maintains, or voluntarily participates' inside quote marks, rather than reproducing it verbatim or using reported speech outside the quote marks.
recommendations: File a corrections record addressing both items above.
In future submissions, either drop unverifiable parenthetical expansions/glosses or source them explicitly.

When embedding license/legal text that needs grammatical conversion to fit a sentence, use reported speech outside quote marks or bracket the altered words (e.g. '[files, maintains, or voluntarily participates]') rather than presenting the converted wording as a direct quote.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Strong, well-sourced legal/governance reporting on a live OSI license review. All four named individuals' quotes verified verbatim and correctly attributed to the right person — no conflation between Dolan, Fontana, Schultz, and Chestek despite two of their messages appearing on the same archive page. The one specific mis-paraphrase risk the bot flagged in its own PR description was confirmed caught and excluded. Two minor, non-headline issues (an unsourced acronym gloss and a tense-converted quote) are honestly coverable in a public corrections note; neither undermines the article's central, well-supported thesis. APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS.
